name: Code Bulk Discounts
summary: Shopify app (by Optizio) that turns a discount you have already created into thousands of unique codes and exports them as CSV for email and SMS campaigns.
best_for: shopify stores that already run email or SMS campaigns and need thousands of unique, single-use codes generated out of one existing discount and handed over as a CSV
skip_if: you need one or two codes, which Shopify's own discount screen already gives you at no cost, or the campaign itself is what you want, because this app generates and exports the codes and stops there
honest_knock: Read the free plan's number twice, because the word doing the work is 'lifetime': it is 500 codes in total, not 500 a month. One influencer drop or one email segment can spend the whole allowance in an afternoon, and after that the only way on is $14.99 a month, so the free tier is a sample, not a plan. What the app does is also narrower than the word 'discounts' suggests. It takes a discount you have already created and multiplies it into unique codes you export as a CSV. It does not create the discount rule, does not send the codes to anyone, and does not report which ones were redeemed, so it sits between your discount settings and your email or SMS tool and needs both of those to be worth anything. The one critical review on the listing shows what that costs in practice: when a merchant's parent discount broke after an unrelated change to their stack, every code generated from it went inactive and they learned about it from customers rather than from the app. The developer's answer is the right one to remember (the rules and logic belong to the parent discount, not to Code Bulk) but it means nothing in this app will tell you that a batch has stopped working. The rating also rests on 41 reviews, read 16 September 2026, which is a thin record next to the app's peers.

pricing.notes: (prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/code-bulk and re-verified there on 2026-10-31, unchanged) Two plans, billed in USD every 30 days. Free costs nothing and covers 500 lifetime codes with CSV export. Pro is $14.99 a month and lifts that to unlimited codes per month, with the same CSV export; both plans say they work with most discount applications. The plan table lists no annual rate, no free trial on Pro and no per-code charge, so the monthly figure is the whole cost.

schema_offer.description: Pro per store, per month, billed month-to-month. From our pricing notes: “Pro is $14.99 a month and lifts that to unlimited codes per month” Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-10-31.

free_plan_evidence: Read the free plan's number twice, because the word doing the work is 'lifetime': it is 500 codes in total, not 500 a month.

compare_with.name: Kite
compare_with.why: Both come out of the Shopify discount aisle and both generate bulk codes, but they are priced for different problems. Code Bulk Discounts does one job (turn an existing discount into unique codes and export them) and asks $14.99 a month once the 500 lifetime free codes run out. Kite treats bulk codes as one feature among many and puts them behind $29 a month, with the code ceilings rising by tier. So if codes are the whole requirement, Code Bulk is the cheaper and simpler answer and there is nothing to grow into. If you also want the discount mechanics themselves (free gifts, BOGO, tiered pricing, progress bars) Code Bulk cannot build any of them and Kite is the one that can.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Code Bulk Discounts on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: the plan screens, generating 20 unique codes for a 10 percent discount, the CSV download and the delete dialog. Nothing was paid or deleted. The app opens on Select a discount with the text Search and select an existing discount code, so it does not create a discount rule itself; the list showed only existing discounts. We made a 10 percent order discount in Shopify Discounts first; an Amount off products discount asked for products or collections, so an order discount was used. In the app we searched that discount and chose Generate codes (Automatically generate codes, with the counter 0 of 500 allowance). The form has Count (default 1, set to 20), Charset Alphanumeric, Length 8, empty Prefix and Suffix, Include Job ID (recommended) switched on and a Title, and says Free codes remaining: 500 of 500. After Generate the Previous jobs table showed Requested 20, Imported 0, Failed 0 with Importing 0%, and after about 10 seconds Requested 20, Imported 20, Failed 0 with status Complete. Shopify Discounts then showed 21 codes created by the Shopify web app (the 20 generated plus the main code), each customer entering a unique code, and 0 used. Codes have 8 characters plus the job number as a suffix. The Actions menu offers Download CSV, Connect Klaviyo to upload (greyed out), Email QR embed and Delete Set. Download CSV gave a file with the heading Coupon and 20 codes, all unique; that file is not part of the evidence. Delete Set opened the dialog Delete this set? with Cancel and Delete; Cancel was pressed and nothing was deleted. Timing, approximate tester observations: installation at about 14:22 and the first generated codes at about 14:27, mostly spent choosing the plan and making the parent discount by hand; the code generation itself took 3 steps and about 10 seconds of processing. Not tested: more than 20 codes, Pro, Upload codes, the QR code, Klaviyo, using a code in a real checkout, the app Settings screen and uninstalling. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app does not create a discount rule itself, so a parent discount has to exist in Shopify first; the first attempt, an Amount off products discount, asked for products or collections.

Vendor claim "Search and select an existing discount code". The app then generated 20 codes that Shopify listed as 21 codes with the main code. Plan to create the parent discount in Shopify before generating codes.

Vendor claim "$14,99 / 30 days". What we saw: The Pro plan card shows $14,99 / 30 days with the button Not available because the store is in development. No Pro approval screen, tax, trial or yearly price was seen, so the price could not be checked against a checkout.
